newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower for 4th straight session.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower for 4th straight session.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended lower for a fourth session in a row on Tuesday in slower-than-average trading ahead of mid-August futures index and options settlements, brokers said.

The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 47 most active stocks closed off 0.9 percent at 11,909 points. Total market turnover was 642.2 million reais ($594.6 million), compared with recent daily average of more than one billion reais.
Turnover of the shares in the Bovespa index portfolio totaled 506.2 million reais ($468.7 million).
"With little fresh news out, trade is in the hands of players focusing on the next options and futures expiries," a senior trader said.
Analysts shrugged off Tuesday's news of Brazil's $811 million trade deficit for July, a figure than had been expected since Friday. Before most economists had forecast a much smaller deficit.
Brokers said trading would likely remain slow in the next few days unless there was some unexpected, market-moving news that might push investors such as banks and funds off the sidelines.
